# Overview {#sec-01.0-Section1 .unnumbered}

## Metrics Evaluation

In this section, we delve into the evaluation of various health metrics, focusing on their significance and relevance in assessing public health outcomes. We explore different methodologies and techniques used to evaluate metrics, ensuring a comprehensive understanding of their implications. Through practical examples and case studies, we highlight the importance of robust metrics evaluation in guiding effective health interventions and policy decisions.

### Chapter 1: Introduction to Metrics Evaluation

The Introduction to Metrics Evaluation chapter is a foundational exploration into the world of health metrics, tracing its historical evolution, from the early origins of health measurement to the modern-day methodologies. It provides an overview of the fundamental metrics used in assessing population health, including DALYs (Disability-Adjusted Life Years), HALYs (Healthy Adjusted Life Years), and various other key indicators.

### Chapter 2: Health Metrics

The Health Metrics chapter provides an in-depth analysis of key health indicators, including DALYs (Disability-Adjusted Life Years) and HALYs (Healthy Adjusted Life Years). We explore how these metrics are calculated, their applications in assessing disease burden, and their role in informing health policy. Through discussions and real-world examples, we aim to elucidate the significance of health metrics in measuring population health and guiding resource allocation.

### Chapter 3: Components of the Health Metrics

In this chapter, we break down the components that contribute to health metrics such as DALYs, focusing on understanding the underlying factors driving disease burden. We examine the complex interplay between various components, including mortality, life expectancy, incidence and prevalence, and disability weights, providing insight into their individual and collective impact on population health outcomes. Through comprehensive analysis and case studies, this chapter aims at providing a simple explanation at how to build the components of the health metrics.

### Chapter 4: Causes and Risks

The Causes and Risks chapter investigates the multifaceted nature of health outcomes, exploring the underlying causes and risk factors associated with disease burden. We examine the epidemiological determinants of disease transmission, including infectious agents, environmental factors, and social determinants of health. To identify key drivers of disease burden, enabling the determination of causes and health risks influencing population health outcomes.
